title: Open concept offices aren’t as productive as you think | Your Morning
summary: Morning-show segment on the Harvard open-office study: face-to-face interaction fell and messaging rose after the move.

assertions.quote: the volume of face-to-face interactions so speaking to people that you're now actually sitting across from went down
it's cheaper yeah because it is cheaper

verdicts.note: Cost is a commonly cited motive alongside collaboration goals, but motives are not measured.

Both field sites, like 'many organizations', adopted open architecture with the stated intention of creating more face-to-face interaction, not cutting cost; real-estate motives are not examined, so 'mainly cost' is not supported in these two cases.

assertions.quote: there was more distractions happening because people who are taking personal calls for example you would hear all their business
